narrative.title: The Warehouse Zone Coverage Audit
narrative.scenario: A warehouse's floor plan is encoded as a strip where each position is zone A, B, or C. Compliance requires every audit team to cover a contiguous stretch that touches all three zone types at least once. The planner counts how many distinct stretches qualify — teams differ by where they start and end, not by which zones they see.
narrative.inputFormat: A string s consisting only of 'a', 'b', and 'c'.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the number of substrings that contain at least one 'a', one 'b', and one 'c'.

testCases.explanation: Every stretch ending at index 3 or later qualifies; the count follows each right edge's earliest legal start.
Only stretches that reach the final 'c' and also touch 'a' and 'b' qualify.

hintLevels: Level 1: Fix the right edge and ask how far left the start may sit while still seeing all three letters.
Level 2: Track the latest index of each letter; the minimum of the three is the furthest legal start.
Level 3: Every start position 0..min(last) works, contributing min(last)+1 substrings per right edge.
